script.text: Whenever someone asks me what I do for work, my soul quietly leaves my body for about four seconds.
Because normal people have real jobs. They do marketing, or finance, or they fix things. And then it's my turn, and I have to look an adult in the eyes and say... I draw cartoons on the internet.
And immediately, they give you that polite little nod. The one that means: 'Oh... so you're unemployed.'
And the embarrassing part is... on paper, they're right. My total earnings this month? Zero dollars and zero cents.
I even set up a Ko-fi page. Just a little tip jar in case anyone wanted to support my work. But hardly anyone actually donates.
And it hurts, because I'm not slacking off. I spend forty hours a week hunched over my tablet, animating frame by frame. But to the outside world, it just looks like I'm wasting my time.
And what's scary is... late at night, I wonder if they're right. YouTube is getting stricter, views are low, and people move on so fast.
What if I pour years into this and never make it? What if this whole dream is just a very elaborate way to avoid growing up?
I don't have a grand answer. I'm still terrified. But even with zero views and zero dollars... I still care about this. So I'm going to draw the next frame anyway.
